findings.claim: Actual public files/APIs recover DGI2025 for 22 targets, GovTech for 33, BREADY expert answers for 18 and latest Enterprise Survey rows for 32. Earlier access gaps are solved at this level.
BREADY contains five actual expert procurement-duration questions: 90 target-country cells, 56 plain numeric. Annotated median/skip strings retained rather than coerced.
GovTech December2025 has 198 country-code rows but Nicaragua is a hyphen placeholder: 197 assessed economies. Workbook documents survey/remote-review mix and AI-assisted validation.

Current public Enterprise Survey payment variable is bready_reg9; filters must exclude subnational Location rows. Numeric payment values exist for 31 target countries in the fetched latest-wave response.

Actual OCDS sample has 12 linked award/signature records, one negative difference, and eight dated approval milestones; all eight dateMet equal dueDate and three precede signing. These are not verified final-delivery durations.
Current agreement index is explicitly a modelling choice, not a fitted implementation probability.
Procurement event retrieval is possible, but release timestamps, actual decisions, plans and transactions require separate interpretation and quality checks.
OECD/WB indices provide administrative context, not a calibrated probability that a specific safeguard will operate by June 2027.
The OECD 200-case study explicitly disclaims generalisability to the broader government-AI universe; case counts cannot serve as global adoption denominators.
PSTW, ATRS and Epoch support named-system/model/cluster discovery; they do not establish a common exhaustive risk-exposure population.
Technical intervention efficacy can be measured on a specified test distribution; transporting it to procurement, finance or regulatory route efficacy needs additional evidence.
Media-discovered and LLM-enriched incident reports are not a direct measure of risk reduction or remedy effect.

Proposal: use one prespecified implementation event for x, and either common audited exposure reach or outcome-specific incremental harms for y. Do not normalise unlike denominators merely to obtain 0–1 values.
Bounded exact-form and broader implementation searches did not identify calibration for 1/(1+N); this is not proof no relevant data exist.

recommendation.x: Common target: probability that the exact safeguard is enforceable and operational before a fixed June 2027 checkpoint, conditional on present stage and elapsed time. Build actual event histories and comparable reference classes with cancellation/rejection as competing events; validate calibration out of time and jurisdiction. Keep adoption, operation and witnessed remedy test separate. No numeric prediction until support exists; handoff count remains a descriptor.
recommendation.y: Prefer verified safeguard reach in one fixed audited deployment/exposure population as a narrower measurable axis, explicitly labelled reach. True consequential impact requires outcome-specific counterfactual harm reduction conditional on implementation. Do not combine capacity, dollars, document counts or local-pool percentages. Keep technical efficacy separate from policy-induced uptake and exposure.
